details:
By the defaults, mobile builds block poor or worse avatars, while the PC version will show everything by default.

I find this questionable, even if you have a good computer, the first thing you need to do is add in some limits.

Both PC and mobile should ship with reasonable defaults that you can later override.

Starting with blocking poor or worse avatars is a good start, and should probably be the default on PC as well.

But I believe this is not aggressive enough, there are other options that can be deployed, namely the avatar file size limits and avatar culling.

As for PC avatar file size, anyone that knows Canny 101 knows that the world revolves around the poster, and as such as I'm going to use my own avatar as benchmark for what is a reasonable size limit.

Let A be the average file size and B be the standard deviation. First column compressed second uncompressed. A reasonable starting point would then be:

10 20{⍺×⌈⍵÷⍺}3×A+3×B

AKA: Take the average avatar size, add three standard deviations, multiply the result by three, and round upward to the nearest 10 MB for compressed size or 20 MB for uncompressed size.

With 2 decimal places, since that is what the UI reports:

A = 2.08 8.80

B = 1.25 4.84

And as such

10 20{⍺×⌈⍵÷⍺}3×A+3×B => 20 80

This 20 MB compressed, 80 MB uncompressed limit is of course a starting value that can be overridden later.

In addition, avatar culling should probably be set to a default on all platform to:

Hide avatar further away than: 15 meters

Maximum shown avatars: 10

The 15-meter distance is based on voice falloff. With audio reaching zero at 25 meters and already being difficult to hear at 15 meters, there is generally little reason to automatically render full avatars beyond that distance for ordinary social interaction.
title: Reasonable performance blocking defaults
